title: Dynamic-range panorama weaving and sky-driven color grading in drone post-processing
summary: The video is a practical studio-style walkthrough of post-processing drone panoramas, focusing on expanding dynamic range, stitching multiple exposures into a seamless panorama, and then sculpting light and color to emphasize sky, architecture, and foreground subjects. The presenter discusses RAW processing, exposure management to protect highlights, and manual warp-based alignment to preserve straight lines while avoiding distortion. He demonstrates sky-specific edits (whites adjustments in RAW, gradient color grading, selective color tuning, and occasional blur) and then moves to painting light across the scene—behind a tower, across palm trees, and along beams—to create depth and a three-dimensional feel. The workflow also covers edge cleanups, flower/foreground refinements, brush-based blends (soft vs. hard brushes), clone-like edits, and final touches with dehaze, Orton/blur diffusion, and selective emphasis to direct the viewer’s eye. Throughout, the emphasis is on iterative, brush-based adjustments rather than automated selections, with caveats about exposure, weather conditions, and file handling evident in the narration.

sections.title: Dynamic range expansion and RAW exposure management; panorama prep
sections.description: The presenter expands the dynamic range across files while dropping exposure slightly to keep highlights in check, noting drone DR improvements and underexposure considerations. This sets up the subsequent panorama workflow and prepares the frames for merging.

sections.title: Panorama stitching and distortion control; warp-based alignment
sections.description: Discussion of merging multiple exposures into a panorama, critique of overlap (DJI’s typical ~30% overlap), and the use of warps to influence distortion and alignment, with emphasis on consistent warping across shots.

sections.title: Sky emphasis and edge handling; initial sky edits
sections.description: The shot with challenging upper edges prompts the use of a blur strategy for the sky, followed by careful edge work to keep lines straight and avoid distorting beams or trunks. The presenter emphasizes controlled warping and edge fidelity during sky manipulation.

sections.title: Lighting emphasis and color control via RAW and HSL
sections.description: A focus on pulling detail from the sky and beams through RAW whites adjustments, followed by targeted HSL adjustments for palm trees and a staged color gradient to shape the overall mood without disturbing the sky’s integrity.

sections.title: Orton/dehaze approach and HDR consideration for beams
sections.description: The presenter debates Orton vs dehaze diffusion for background luminosity, demonstrates subtle HDR-like beam enhancement, and discusses managing background glow while preserving foreground clarity.

sections.title: Perspective warp and foreground cleanups; composition refinements
sections.description: Perspective warping and targeted crops are used to align the composition, with manual edge work to remove stray elements and to guide the viewer’s eye toward light sources and strong lines.

sections.title: Final touches: RAW profile quirks, brush-based refinements, and punchy sky
sections.description: The sequence covers matching exposures across frames, handling odd RAW profiles, and using deliberate brush work to blend gradients, pop specific features (beams, tower sides), and finalize the image with careful color grading, brightness shifts, and a subtle vignette.
